title: Some Unique Places

standard_text: Unique natural and cultural places of India and what makes them special; heritage sites and how to protect them; reading a map using directions, the key and the scale; responsible tourism (summary of NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 6).

body_html:
How to think about it

India has many unique places: the living root bridges of Meghalaya, the floating phumdis of Loktak Lake, the white salt Rann of Kutch, the coral islands of Lakshadweep and the river island Majuli. Heritage sites such as the Taj Mahal, Hampi, the Konark Sun Temple and the Ajanta caves tell us about the past.

Maps help us find these places: north is usually at the top, the key explains the symbols and the scale compares map distance with real distance. We protect heritage sites by not writing on walls, using dustbins and following the rules.

Example

Floating islands called phumdis are in…

Manipur

Answer: Loktak Lake

Example

Kolkata is ___ of Mumbai.

look at the map

Answer: east

Common mistakes

  • Writing names on monuments.
  • Thinking north is wherever you face.
  • Mixing up natural and cultural heritage.
